reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it chiefly reviews Terra/LUNA's stablecoin mechanism, payment ambitions, roadmap, and staking model. The creator is enthusiastic and discusses potential rewards, but does not promise a guaranteed return or direct viewers to send money or private data to a destination. The creator also identifies a drawback and encourages viewers to read the white paper.

opening.argument: Judge, the profit discussion supplies a participation path. Viewers hear that investors “can buy and hold Luna,” then that a holder can swap LUNA for UST and sell it “for more than a dollar, making a profit.” The explanation goes further, saying holders see LUNA's value rise during expansion. Taken together, these are not just descriptions of payment technology; they connect acquiring a token to two potential financial rewards.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this education and points to the disclaimer, but “not financial advice” does not erase the described buy-and-hold route to profit. Nor does mentioning volatility change the way the embedded explanation presents a holder's opportunity to sell above a dollar. The question is how the financial opportunity is conveyed, not whether the speaker issues a direct command to send funds.

citations.quote: this is just information used for information and educational purposes only this is not financial advice.
any LUNA holder can swap $1 worth of LUNA for one UST and sell each UST for more than a dollar, making a profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those quotes describe a conditional mechanism, not an assured gain: buying and holding is attributed to investors who predict future use, and the swap example applies when UST rises above its peg. The speaker also identifies short-term volatility as a risk borne by stakers. The cited material does not show the creator instructing viewers to buy LUNA or promising that the stated conditions will occur.

If you're staking your Terra Luna you're going to be rewarded staking fees because you assume short term volatility and taking on that risk.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the reward language in combination. The speaker says staking Terra LUNA will earn fees, while the embedded explanation says holders who stake earn transaction fees and describes earning “passive income.” It also presents validators as receiving a “steady cash flow of UST” even when demand is low. Although volatility is acknowledged, that repeated emphasis on income makes staking sound like a dependable way to be paid. The warning should not outweigh the cumulative appeal of those claims.

citations.quote: If you're staking your Terra Luna you're going to be rewarded staking fees because you assume short term volatility and taking on that risk.
Investors who hold Loona see its value raise during times of expansion, and, if they choose to stake, earn transaction fees on UST.
Even when demand for UST is low, Terra's algorithm automatically increases fees so that validators are always rewarded with a steady cash flow of UST
with LUNA, you can do so much more than earn passive income

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites volatility as proof of balance. Yet the same discussion pairs that risk with the assurance that staking earns fees, and the embedded explanation says validators are “always rewarded” with steady cash flow. Reading the risk disclosure alone understates how strongly the rewards are foregrounded.

citations.quote: If you're staking your Terra Luna you're going to be rewarded staking fees because you assume short term volatility and taking on that risk.
validators are always rewarded with a steady cash flow of UST

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The strongest reward wording concerns validators' fees, not a guaranteed net return to every viewer. Staking is presented as optional, and the speaker explicitly says stakers assume short-term volatility and risk. The cited statements establish discussion of how participation may be compensated; they do not establish a deceptive promise of fixed or risk-free income.

If you're staking your Terra Luna you're going to be rewarded staking fees because you assume short term volatility and taking on that risk.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing also functions as a pitch for the token. The title calls Terra “The next paypal”; the speaker calls it a “really good project,” says it is “disrupting,” and relays a named investor's recommendation of LUNA. The video then gives the audience the financial premise for holding it: rising usefulness can motivate buying LUNA, and holders may benefit during expansion. That sequence makes the favorable review more than a neutral explanation of a stablecoin.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes the white-paper invitation and the speaker's criticism of a merchant fee. Those details show the speaker reviewed the project, but they do not neutralize the praise, the reported recommendation, or the buy-and-hold premise. A pitch can include reservations and still steer an audience toward viewing a token as an opportunity.

The buying passage is conditional on an investor's prediction of future usefulness. The prosecution's quotes show favorable commentary about LUNA, but not a guaranteed appreciation claim or a request that viewers purchase it.
